description: OLMoE-1B-7B-0924-Instruct Q4_K_M decode on one RTX 4080 SUPER: llama.cpp b12024 vs DeepInfer scripts/bench_olmoe_decode.py, three interleaved rounds in one session, plus greedy top-5 logits from both engines and a CUPTI per-kernel breakdown. See docs/OLMOE_PORT_PLAN.md section 37.

environment.gpu: NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4080 SUPER 32 GB (SM89), driver 580.105.08
environment.cpu: Intel Xeon Platinum 8352V @ 2.10GHz, 128 visible threads, cgroup quota 16 CPUs

llamacpp.note: built from a tarball, so llama-bench reports build_commit 'unknown'

deepinfer.remote_tree: 120 tracked sources under deepinfer/, kernels/, tests/moe and scripts/bench_olmoe_decode.py identical to HEAD (CRLF-normalised sha256)

notes: cpu_probe_ms in rounds[].runs[] is taken by the driver process right after it idled; it reads 37-56 ms even when the probe inside the busy benchmark process reads 21-25 ms, so only deepinfer_bench.records[].repeat_cpu_probe_ms identifies the host's slow state.

Kernel categories come from CUPTI traces with tracing on; DeepInfer's traced busy time is 4.11 ms against 4.02 ms untraced, and llama.cpp's traced tg64 fell to 439 tok/s, so only kernel durations are used from the traces, not end-to-end speed.
